old_caption: The video captures a controlled burn in a grassy area. The camera, likely mounted on a person's helmet or body, provides a first-person perspective. Initially, the focus is on flames consuming dry grass and small branches near a wooden structure, possibly a platform or fence. As the camera pans right, more of the landscape is revealed, showing rolling hills covered in dry vegetation. The sky above is partly cloudy. The fire continues to spread, casting an orange glow and billowing smoke into the air, partially obscuring the view. The camera movement follows the fire's progression across the terrain. No animals or other characters are visible, emphasizing the isolation and scale of the landscape. The overall atmosphere reflects the process of land management through fire.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene of controlled burning in a grassy area. The camera, likely mounted on a person's helmet or body, provides a first-person perspective. Initially, the focus is on the flames consuming dry grass and small branches near a wooden structure, possibly a platform or a fence. As the camera pans to the right, it reveals more of the landscape, showing a vast expanse of rolling hills covered in similar dry vegetation. The sky above is partly cloudy, suggesting a cool day. The fire continues to spread, casting an orange glow over the area, while smoke billows into the air, partially obscuring the view. The camera movement is smooth, following the natural progression of the fire as it moves across the terrain. There are no visible animals or other characters in the frame, emphasizing the isolation and scale of the landscape. The overall atmosphere is one of controlled destruction, highlighting the process of land management through fire.
caption: The video captures a steep hillside of dry grass actively burning, with orange flame patches flickering along the slope and smoke rising into the hazy air. An elevated wooden platform on posts and a concrete footing fills the upper view, while a dark blurred object intrudes at the right edge. The flames shift shape continuously as thin smoke drifts upward and partially veils the slope. Initially the framing sits close to the burning grass. A bright flame patch on the left appears alongside central and lower flames. As the clip proceeds the view shifts upward, revealing more of the platform and the pale hills beyond, while the left flame patch leaves the view. The central and lower flames remain visible throughout, their tongues bending and rising. The apparent movement of the fire within the view tracks the changing viewpoint rather than a clear advance of the burn. The view ends with the hillside still burning and the structure in view, leaving the fire's cause and progression outside the visible scene.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
